newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bank sees economic advance in 97.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bank sees economic advance in 97.

text.p: Moroccan bank Banque Commerciale du Maroc said in its annual report that money supply growth in 1997 would not go beyond six or seven percent which would limit inflation to the level of the previous year.
Inflation last year was three percent and the bank's forecast echoed one made on Tuesday by the Moroccan Statistics Directorate that it would be similar in 1997.

In its report just released, BCM said its forecast took account of a three percent increase in Gross Domestic Product excluding agriculture although growth remained widely dependent on a harvest expected to be below last year's output.
The bank said among prospects for 1997 were reforms of the Stock Exchange which plans the creation of a central depository and a secondary market.
BCM said that Morocco last year had benefited from an exceptional harvest, with GDP rising 11.8 percent.
Foreign direct investments in 1996 reached $750 million compared to $450 million in 1995, the bank said.
